messages:
Amanda (Sales): Heads-up — FinServ pilot is greenlit for a 3-week POC. They want an ops plan for capacity + a pricing estimate before legal signs the commit. Traffic profile: ~800 concurrent user sessions, average response ~450 tokens, steady-state qps ~12, but short spikes up to 80 qps for ~5–12m. p95 latency target <= 500ms. Also flagged security Qs (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Can we recommend a reserved setup + autoscale policy to meet SLOs while keeping cost predictable?

Ben (Platform): Thanks. Short answer: reserve for steady-state baseline and allow short burst capacity. For those spikes we'd use a small burst pool + aggressive batching and prefix caching. Two follow-ups: which model family (LlamaX-70B quant vs LLM-lite-13B) and where is the POC hosted (hosted vs dedicated)? That changes GPU counts.

Amanda (Sales): Customer prefers open models and wants hosted API for velocity. They're OK with quantized variants if accuracy stays within their eval set.

Devon (SE): Given hosted + quantized 13B, rough plan: reserve capacity sized for steady qps * concurrency factor, plus a burst pool sized to absorb 95th pct spikes. Proposal: reserve 8 GPUs (A100xlarge equiv) for baseline, plus 3 GPU burst pool with preemptive warmers. Prewarming + KV prefix cache should keep p95 low. For check-in: we'll run a synthetic traffic replay first 48h to validate.

Luca (SRE): Important: session affinity for long multi-turn sessions — otherwise cache hits drop and latency jumps. Also recommend per-route SLO routing: route low-latency endpoints to reserved pool and background rerank/embeds to shared cheaper pool.

Devon (SE): Example autoscale policy (first draft):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  baseline_gpus: 8
  burst_pool: 3
  scale_up_threshold_qps: 40   # if sustained > 40 qps for 2m
  scale_down_threshold_qps: 20 # if below 20 qps for 5m
  warm_margin: 0.15           # keep 15% headroom for sudden surges
  prewarm_triggers:
    - spike_window: 300       # if spike > 60s, prewarm burst nodes
```
This keeps most spikes in the burst pool and avoids cold-starts.

Ben (Platform): Two operational notes: 1) enable continuous batching up to 256 tokens/batch for the 13B quant — increases throughput and smooths token cost; 2) set canary policy for rollouts: canary 10% traffic for 10m, auto-fallback to previous model on error rate >2%.

Amanda (Sales): Pricing ask from FinServ: "what's the monthly commitment for the reserve above, and can we show an example bill for 1M tokens/day?"

Devon (SE): Quick back-of-envelope (hosted, 13B quant): baseline 8 GPUs + 3 burst -> commit ~11 GPUs. Estimated reserved cost: $55k/month (discounted enterprise rate). Token run-rate: with batching/caching ~1M tokens/day -> ~30M tokens/month -> ballpark $3.2k–$4.5k extra in usage (depends on cache hit). If they push heavy long-context sessions, add ~20% headroom. I'll prepare a slide with sensitivities.

Luca (SRE): Security bits: confirm KMS integration for key rotation, customer-managed VPC peering, and audit logs retention 90d. For SOC2 questions we can provide our compliance pack; legal may need a signature timeframe estimate 5–7 business days.

Amanda (Sales): Perfect. Can we also document failure modes for the commit? Customer wants explicit rollback and SLA behavior during region outage.

Ben (Platform): Failure modes doc (short):
- Region outage: traffic routed to secondary region; if capacity insufficient we fall back to smaller model variant with 2x latency but preserved throughput.
- Burst pool saturates: queue backpressure applied and requests that exceed SLO go to soft-fail with explanatory error for the app to retry.
- Cold starts: prewarming + persistent KV cache minimizes this; worst-case p95 degrades to ~900ms for 90s.

Devon (SE): I'll draft a 1-pager describing the POC runbook: traffic replay, monitoring dashboards (p95, tokens, batch size), canary windows, rollback steps, and a cost sensitivity table.

infra-bot: created runbook:POC-FS-178002 by Devon. Link: https://redwood.ops/poc/POC-178002

Amanda (Sales): Awesome — Devon/Ben, can you have commit sizing + price slide + 1-pager ready for the customer kickoff on Monday? I'll share the security pack after Legal confirms timeline. :thumbsup:

Ben (Platform): Yep — will sync and post slides by EOD Friday.

Devon (SE): On it. I'll include the traffic replay harness and the sample autoscaler config so EngOps can apply it quickly.

Luca (SRE): I'll attach suggested Grafana dashboard JSON and alert thresholds (p95 > 500ms, queue_length > 50) before the kickoff.

Amanda (Sales): Thanks team. I'll keep FinServ updated.
